episode_title: What AI does to language and culture with Sabine Harnau and Holger Schueler

real_qa.q: What does Common Crawl training data reveal about AI language model bias toward English?
real_qa.r: Around 45% of Common Crawl is English, and as of October last year, English was used by almost half of all websites on the internet. The training data shows that AI models' default is American professional class English, creating a significant imbalance where Spanish is second at around 6% and German is a close runner-up in single digits.
real_qa.requete: Common Crawl English percentage AI training data

real_qa.q: How does AI language model training differ from human child language acquisition?
real_qa.r: AI doesn't learn language the way a child would during language acquisition, where they try themselves out and copy what grown-ups are doing. Instead, AI training goes through statistical likelihoods, producing words that are likely to appear next, which relies on huge amounts of training data rather than interactive experimentation.
real_qa.requete: AI language learning vs child language acquisition difference

real_qa.q: What does the paper 'The Ghost in the Machine Has an American Accent' reveal about LLM bias?
real_qa.r: This 2022 pre-print paper (not yet peer-reviewed) demonstrates that when you look at what AI produces, especially when used in English, the model's default is American professional class English. It shows how cultural and linguistic biases are embedded in large language models through their training data sources.
real_qa.requete: Ghost in the Machine American Accent AI paper 2022

real_qa.q: Why did Google Meet prioritize English and Spanish for live machine interpretation over other languages?
real_qa.r: When Google Meet offered live machine interpretation, the first languages supported were English and Spanish because those are the very important languages in the US, reflecting how product rollout decisions reflect US-centric priorities rather than global language needs.
real_qa.requete: Google Meet live interpretation English Spanish why first

real_qa.q: What is the significance of Bible translations as training data for under-resourced languages in AI models?
real_qa.r: In under-resourced languages, almost the only text available is religious text, particularly the Bible, which is easy to use for training language models because it has very clearly separated parts of text that neatly align across different languages, creating biases in how AI understands these languages.
real_qa.requete: Bible translation AI training under-resourced languages

guest.bio_context: Sabine started From Scratch Communications in 2017 in the UK and moved it to the Netherlands in 2018. She studied cultural studies and linguistics plus educational psychology at university. She worked as a copywriter in an agency before founding her agency, and her background also includes work in teaching, where she appreciated the balance between stable structure and freedom to adapt to different students and challenges.
